case_number: 2025 INSC 151; CRIMINAL APPEAL NO(S). OF 2025 (ARISING OUT OF SLP(CRL.) NO(S). 15882 OF 2024)
summary: Summoning order challenged; consent vs rape on promise of marriage; initial consensual relationship; no misconception of fact established; false promise vs breach of promise distinguished; Uday and Deepak Gulati cited; prosecution failed to prove absence of consent; burden on prosecution; charges under IPC and SC/ST Act examined; ongoing relationship despite relocation; pregnancy and-abortion not coerced per record; caste-based abuse allegations noted; father's summoning quashed by HC; appeal by accused against own summoning; lack of mala fide in early stages not shown; judicial scrutiny of consent in promise-to-marry cases emphasized; context, intent, and surrounding circumstances relevant; consent remains valid unless vitiated by fraud or deceit at inception.
legal_provisions_cited: Indian Penal Code, 1860 s.376, s.323, s.504, s.506, s.313
Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 s.3(1)(r), s.3(1)(s), s.3(2)(5a), s.3(2)(v), s.3(1)(d), s.3(2)(va)
Deepak Gulati v. State of Haryana
final_judgment: Appeal allowed in part; summoning order against appellant upheld; High Court's partial quashing upheld; no interference with trial against Manish Yadav; proceedings to continue before trial court.
